# Volume 3 — Chapter XV A Dream Turned Upside Down

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Only one week remains before our return to Wexcombe,” Nell remarked. The prospect of resuming her job, her studies, and her social life in Wexcombe brought her joy. Delightful images were likewise forming in her mind regarding Tabby’s Place. Thinking about it imparted a cozy, agreeable feeling of home, despite her having never resided there.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0000 }

Yet that summer had likewise brought immense happiness—a period defined by joyful existence under warm suns and bright skies, an era of sharp pleasure derived from wholesome pursuits; a season marked by the refreshing and strengthening of established friendships; an interval during which she had acquired the ability to exist with greater nobility, to labor with increased patience, and to engage in recreation with a fuller heart.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0001 }

“Not every lesson in life is taught in college,” it occurred to her. “They are taught by life in all places.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0002 }

However, to Nell's dismay, that lovely holiday's last seven days were ruined by a mischievous event resembling a inverted nightmare.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0003 }

“Have you written any other tales recently?” asked Mr. Pettifer pleasantly one night as Nell shared tea with Mrs. Pettifer and him.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0004 }

“No,” Nell replied, in a somewhat crisp tone.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0005 }

“Well, I did not mean to offend. Not long ago, Mrs. Hiram Mott informed me that four weeks back, a large envelope directed to the Rollings Reliable Baking Powder Company of Montreal was deposited in the post office box, and she suspected that a person was competing for the award they had advertised for the top tale that incorporated the name of their baking powder. She mentioned that the handwriting on the address was not yours, yet I supposed perhaps you were the one.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0006 }

“Certainly not! Although the prize offer came to my attention, competing for it is something I would never consider. Writing a tale for the purpose of promoting a baking powder strikes me as completely shameful. Such an act would be nearly as dreadful as the patent medicine fence belonging to Judson Tibbs.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0007 }

Nell spoke thus in a haughty manner, completely unaware of the humbling experience that lay ahead for her. During that exact evening, Isolde, her eyes sparkling and her cheeks flushed, darted into the porch gable bearing a missive.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0008 }

“Oh, Nell, a letter has arrived for you. Since I happened to be at the office, I decided to hand-deliver it myself. Hurry up and open it. Should it turn out to be the news I am anticipating, my joy will be absolutely boundless.” Perplexed, Nell unsealed the message and scanned the typed lines inside.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0009 }

The address was for Miss Nell Harcourt, located at Grey Shutters in Brierley on St. Brendan’s Island.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0010 }

“DEAR MADAM: It gives us great delight to let you know that a prize of twenty-five dollars, offered in our late contest, has been awarded to your delightful tale ‘Evadne’s Atonement’. Included here is the check. Plans are being made by us to publish the narrative across a number of well-known Canadian journals, and it is our further purpose to produce it as a pamphlet to hand out to our clientele. Expressing our gratitude for your engagement with our project,
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0011 }

“We are, “Most truly yours, “THE ROLLINGS RELIABLE BAKING POWDER CO.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0012 }

“I do not comprehend,” Nell stated, with a blank expression.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0013 }

Isolde struck her palms together.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0014 }

“Oh, I was certain it would take the prize—I knew it would. Nell, I submitted your story to the contest.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0015 }

“Isolde—Pembroke!”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0016 }

“Yes, I did,” Isolde said with glee, settling on top of the bed. “The moment I noticed the offer, I immediately remembered your story, and my initial thought was to have you submit it yourself. However, I worried you might refuse, given how little confidence you still had in it. Therefore, I resolved to mail the copy you provided me without uttering a word about it. That way, had it missed out on the prize, you would remain unaware and avoid feeling hurt, as unsuccessful manuscripts were not going to be sent back, whereas if it succeeded, it would be a wonderful shock for you.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0017 }

Although Isolde was not a mortal of great discernment, at that very second she realized that Nell failed to appear entirely thrilled. Unquestionably, she saw the astonishment—yet where had the joy gone?
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0018 }

“Why, Nell, you do not appear the least bit glad!” she cried out.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0019 }

Nell immediately fabricated a smile and wore it.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0020 }

“Naturally, your generous desire to bring me joy could only make me happy,” she uttered unhurriedly. “However, you must realize—I am utterly astonished—it seems surreal to me—and it makes no sense. Not a single mention appeared in my tale regarding—regarding—” Nell gagged slightly on the term—“baking powder.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0021 }

“Oh, I inserted that,” Isolde stated, feeling comforted. “It was completely effortless—and naturally, my former time in our old Story Club gave me an advantage. You remember the part when Evadne bakes the cake? Well, I simply mentioned that she incorporated Rollings Reliable into the recipe, which explained why it was such a success; and after that, during the final paragraph, when Perceval holds Evadne tight in his arms and utters, ‘Sweetheart, the beautiful coming years will bring us the fulfilment of our home of dreams,’ I appended, ‘in which we will never use any baking powder except Rollings Reliable.’”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0022 }

“Oh,” miserable Nell gasped, resembling a person who had been splashed with chilly water.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0023 }

“And the twenty-five dollars belong to you,” Isolde added with jubilation. “Why, it was stated by Honora on one occasion that a story brings merely five dollars from the Canadian Woman!”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0024 }

In trembling fingers, Nell offered the dreadful pink slip.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0025 }

“I am unable to accept it—it belongs to you by right, Isolde. You submitted the story and executed the changes. I—I definitely would not ever have submitted it. Therefore, you have to accept the check.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0026 }

“It would amuse me to see that,” Isolde remarked with disdain. “Really, my actions required no effort whatsoever. Having the privilege to be connected to the winner of the prize satisfies me completely. Anyhow, it is time for my departure. My journey should have taken me directly back to my house after visiting the post office, considering visitors are present. Even so, learning what happened was something I just could not resist doing. Your good fortune brings me immense joy, Nell.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0027 }

Nell abruptly leaned toward her, wrapped her arms around Isolde, and pressed her lips to her cheek.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0028 }

“Isolde, I believe you are the world's most genuine and dearest friend,” she stated, her voice quivering slightly, “and I guarantee that I value the reason behind your actions.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0029 }

Feeling a mixture of delight and self-consciousness, Isolde departed, whereupon miserable Nell threw the harmless check into her bureau drawer like it was a payoff for murder, before throwing herself onto her bed to cry tears born of humiliation and wounded feelings. Oh, she would fail to ever move past this—fail completely!
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0030 }

It was dusk when Hugh arrived, overflowing with well-wishes because he had dropped by Pear Hill and learned what had happened. However, the moment he saw Nell’s face, his congratulations withered away.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0031 }

“Why, Nell, what has happened? I anticipated seeing you beaming with joy about taking home the Rollings Reliable award. Well done!”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0032 }

“Oh, Hugh, not you,” pleaded Nell, sounding like someone crying et-tu Brute. “I believed you were going to comprehend. Is it not possible for you to perceive the terrible nature of it?”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0033 }

“I have to admit I am unable to. What is the issue?”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0034 }

“Everything,” Nell groaned. “It feels to me like I am shamed for all time. How do you suppose a mother would react if she discovered her youngster covered in tattoos for a baking powder ad? That is precisely how I feel. My poor little tale was dear to me, and I penned it from the finest part of my soul. Having it dragged down to the degree of a baking powder ad is a desecration. Do you recall what Professor Hamilton was accustomed to saying to us during the literature course at Regent’s? We were never to compose one word from a mean or dishonorable impulse, so he stated, but were perpetually to hold fast to the utmost standards. What is his opinion going to be when it comes to his ears that I have authored a tale to market Rollings Reliable? And, oh, once the news spreads at Wexcombe! Imagine the way I will be mocked and ridiculed!”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0035 }

“You certainly will not,” Hugh stated, anxiously pondering whether it was specifically the view of that wretched Junior that caused Nell such concern. “The Reds are going to assume precisely what occurred to me—that since you lack an abundance of material riches, as is true for nine in ten among our group, you chose this method to make a legitimate income to assist with your annual expenses. Nothing about it strikes me as cheap, disgraceful, or even laughable. Naturally, a person would prefer producing literary triumphs—yet in the interim, room, food, and class costs demand payment.”
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0036 }

The practical, logical perspective on the situation gave Nell a bit of comfort. It served to eliminate her fear that she would be mocked, even if the more profound pain of a violated ideal persisted.
{: #nw-v03-c15-p0037 }
